doc.title: Lanny Morgan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

title: Giving up medicine for music after hearing City College's sax section
summary: Planning to be a doctor, he heard Bob McDonald's saxes rehearsing and was won over by bebop.

bands.name: Los Angeles City College Jazz Band

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Did you have any aspirations of being a professional musician as a senior in high school?

At the very end I did because actually I had a math/science major all through school. I was going to be a doctor but that didn’t really go too well really. I wasn’t — it just didn’t appeal to me that much, the classes or the prospect of being in medicine really. So I was in all the all-city and all-state orchestras out here on violin, and they used to rehearse at City College. And we would get there sometimes, and Bob McDonald, who I didn’t know then, would keep maybe the sax section or the brass section from his radio and recording orchestra over for a little section rehearsal. So we had to wait for them to get through. And one day I heard this — he had kept the sax section over and I heard that and it just blew me away and that was it. And I kept up the violin for a little while, I kept up the pretense I guess. But I mean actually I was a pretty good fiddle player. I’d gone through all the literature, never played professionally, but it was a little difficult to give it
up but the pull was so strong from what was called bebop at that time, that I couldn’t fight it.
